[[EuroLeague]] | team = Real Madrid | birth_date = {{Birth date and age|2002|3|9|df=y}} | birth_place = [[Madrid]], Spain | nationality = Spanish | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | draft_league = | career_start = 2017 | years1 = 2017–present | team1 = [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] | years2 = 2017–2019 | team2 = →[[Real Madrid Baloncesto B|Real Madrid B]] | highlights = * [[EuroLeague Rising Star]] ([[2020–21 EuroLeague|2021]]) * [[ACB Best Young Player Award|ACB Best Young Player]] ([[2020–21 ACB season|2021]]) * 2× [[ACB Best Young Player Award|ACB All-Young Players Team]] ([[2019–20 ACB season|2020]], 2021) * [[Liga ACB]] champion ([[2018–19 ACB season|2019]]) * [[Supercopa de España de Baloncesto|Supercopa]] winner ([[2020 Supercopa de España de Baloncesto|2020]]) * [[Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament|EB Next Generation Tournament]] champion ([[2018–19 Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament|2019]]) * [[FIBA U16 European Championship]] MVP ([[2016 FIBA U16 European Championship|2016]]) | medaltemplates = {{MedalSport|Men's basketball}} {{MedalCountry|{{bk|ESP}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA U18 European Championship]]}} {{MedalGold|[[2019 FIBA U18 European Championship|2019 Greece]]|[[Spain national under-18 basketball team|Team]]}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA U16 European Championship]]}} {{MedalGold|[[2016 FIBA U16 European Championship|2016 Poland]]|[[Spain national under-16 basketball team|Team]]}} {{MedalSilver|[[2018 FIBA U16 European Championship|2018 Serbia]]|[[Spain national under-16 basketball team|Team]]}} }} '''Destiny Usman Garuba Alari''' (born 9 March 2002) is a Spanish professional [[basketball]] player for [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] of the [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroLeague]]. Listed at {{height|m=2.03}}, he plays the [[center (basketball)|center]] position. Garuba was born in [[Madrid]], Spain to Nigerian parents and joined the youth academy of Real Madrid at age 11. In 2019, when he was 17 years old, he became the youngest starter in Real Madrid history. In the 2020–21 season, Garuba was named [[EuroLeague Rising Star]] and [[ACB Best Young Player Award|ACB Best Young Player]]. He earned [[most valuable player]] (MVP) honors at the [[2016 FIBA U16 European Championship]] at age 14. == Early life and youth career == Born in Hospital 12 de Octubre in [[Madrid]], Garuba was raised in the neighborhood of [[Villaverde Alto (Madrid)|Villaverde Alto]] and the municipality of [[Azuqueca de Henares]] (province of Guadalajara).{{cite web |last1=Gonzalez |first1=Raquel |title=¿Quién es Usman Garuba? El madridista que manda en Europa |url=https://as.com/baloncesto/2018/08/12/mas_baloncesto/1534074312_747506.html |website=[[Diario AS]] |access-date=10 October 2019 |language=es |date=27 July 2019}}{{cite web |last1=del Río |first1=César |title=Usman Garuba, la perla del Real Madrid de baloncesto que salió de la cantera del Azuqueca |url=http://www.encastillalamancha.es/deportes/usman-garuba-la-perla-del-real-madrid-baloncesto-salio-la-cantera-del-azuqueca/ |website=encastillalamancha.es |access-date=10 October 2019 |language=es |date=4 November 2017}} He grew up playing [[association football|football]], his original passion, but switched to [[basketball]] because his exceptional height limited his success in the former sport.{{cite web |last1=Hein |first1=David |title=Garuba finally shines for Madrid at ANGT |url=https://www.adidasngt.com/u18/news/latest/i/8pcpwpgll47twfyu/garuba-finally-shines-for-madrid-at-angt |publisher=[[Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament]] |access-date=12 October 2019 |date=29 April 2018}} Garuba idolized former [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) player [[Kareem Abdul-Jabbar]]. In November 2011, he joined Escuela Municipal de Baloncesto de Azuqueca (Municipal Basketball School of Azuqueca), where coach and coordinator David Serrano helped him start his basketball career. In 2013, Garuba joined the lower categories of [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]]. He stood {{height|m=1.89}} and weighed 81 kg (179 lbs) by the time he was 12 years old.{{cite web |title=El "muro" gigante de 12 años del Real Madrid |url=https://www.marca.com/2014/05/28/baloncesto/basketfeb/1401261709.html |website=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]] |access-date=10 October 2019 |language=es |date=28 May 2014}} In 2015, Garuba helped his team win the [[:es:Minicopa Endesa|Minicopa Endesa]], an under-14 Spanish club tournament. He debuted by posting 24 points and 16 rebounds in a win over [[Valencia Basket|Valencia]].{{cite web |title=El coloso infantil del Madrid es la sensación de la Minicopa |url=https://www.marca.com/2015/02/20/baloncesto/copa-rey/1424453935.html |website=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]] |access-date=12 October 2019 |language=es |date=20 February 2015}} In the following year, Garuba led Real Madrid to another Minicopa title and was named MVP of the competition.{{cite web |title=Usman Garuba es el MVP Movistar+ de la Minicopa Endesa |url=http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=120501 |publisher=[[Liga ACB]] |access-date=12 October 2019 |language=es |date=21 February 2016}} He averaged 22.8 rebounds per game in the tournament, grabbing 32 against [[Club Joventut Badalona|Joventut Badalona]] in the final. In February 2018, Garuba gained his first [[Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament|Adidas Next Generation Tournament]] (ANGT) experience with the Real Madrid under-18 team at the [[2017–18 Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament#Munich Tournament|Munich qualifying tournament]], after missing the previous edition with a quadriceps injury. He was selected to the All-Tournament Team, despite being one of the youngest participants. In the final tournament, Garuba averaged 12 points and 6.5 rebounds per game and was named ANGT Rising Star.{{cite web |title=Rytas guard Sirvydis named ANGT MVP |url=https://www.adidasngt.com/u18/news/latest/i/8r35meqnjihofupj/rytas-guard-sirvydis-named-angt-mvp |publisher=[[Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament]] |access-date=13 October 2019 |date=20 May 2018}} In January 2019, he was named MVP of the ANGT Munich tournament after averaging 16.5 points, seven rebounds, and 3.8 assists per game.{{cite web |title=Garuba named MVP of ANGT Munich |url=https://www.adidasngt.com/u18/news/latest/i/9fc8u53ovdvnsmd7/garuba-named-mvp-of-angt-munich |publisher=[[Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament]] |access-date=13 October 2019 |date=27 January 2019}} Garuba helped Real Madrid win the final tournament and joined MVP [[Mario Nakić]] on the All-Tournament Team.{{cite web |last1=Hein |first1=David |title=MVP Nakic of U18 Real Madrid leads Munich all-tourney team |url=https://www.adidasngt.com/u18/news/latest/i/8j6x6vbphcwp7bln/mvp-nakic-of-u18-real-madrid-leads-munich-all-tourney-team |publisher=[[Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament]] |access-date=13 October 2019 |date=11 February 2018}} == Professional career == In the [[2017–18 Liga EBA season|2017–18 season]], Garuba played for [[Real Madrid Baloncesto B|Real Madrid B]], the [[reserve team]] for Real Madrid in the [[Liga EBA]], the [[Spanish basketball league system|fourth-tier]] league in Spain. In 11 games, he averaged 11.1 points, 9.2 rebounds, and 1.7 blocks per game.{{cite web |title=Real Madrid II Statistics - Spanish League |url=https://basketball.eurobasket.com/team/Spain/Real-Madrid-II/2338?Page=3&Stats=2018 |publisher=[[Eurobasket.com]]|access-date=13 October 2019}} In the [[2018–19 Liga EBA season|2018–19 season]], he continued to primarily play for Real Madrid B, averaging 14.6 points, 12.0 rebounds, 2.1 assists, and 1.5 blocks per game over 22 Liga EBA appearances.{{cite web |title=Real Madrid II Statistics - Spanish League |url=https://basketball.eurobasket.com/team/Spain/Real-Madrid-II/2338?Page=3&Stats=2019 |publisher=[[Eurobasket.com]] |access-date=13 October 2019}}{{cite web |title=La semana mágica del MVP Usman Garuba |url=http://www.feb.es/2019/2/4/baloncesto/semana-magica-del-mvp-usman-garuba/77366.aspx |publisher=[[Spanish Basketball Federation]] |access-date=13 October 2019 |language=es |date=4 February 2019}} On 28 October 2018, at 16 years and seven months of age, Garuba debuted for Real Madrid in the [[Liga ACB]], the first-tier league in Spain, against [[CB Miraflores|Miraflores]]. He became the youngest [[center (basketball)|center]] in ACB history, surpassing [[José Ángel Antelo]], and the third-youngest Real Madrid debutant, behind [[Luka Dončić]] and Roberto Núñez.{{cite web |title=Usman Garuba, el pívot más joven en debutar en la Liga Endesa |url=http://www.acb.com/articulo/ver/144180 |publisher=[[Liga ACB]] |access-date=13 October 2019 |language=es |date=28 October 2018}} In the [[2019–20 Real Madrid Baloncesto season|2019–20 season]], Garuba became a full-time member of Real Madrid's senior team. In his season debut against [[Club Joventut Badalona|Joventut Badalona]], at 17 years, six months, and 19 days of age, he eclipsed Dončić as Real Madrid's youngest-ever starter.{{cite web |title=Garuba becomes Real Madrid's youngest-ever starter |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/09/garuba-becomes-real-madrids-youngest-ever-starter |publisher=[[Real Madrid Baloncesto]] |access-date=13 October 2019 |date=28 September 2019}} On 29 September, Garuba recorded 13 points and 10 rebounds in a win over [[CB Murcia|Murcia]] to become the youngest player with a [[double (basketball)|double-double]] or 10 rebounds in ACB history; Dončić had previously held both records. He was also the second-youngest player to post an efficiency rating of 24 in the ACB, behind only [[Ricky Rubio]].{{cite web |title=Liga Endesa ¡Histórico Garuba! Supera los récords de precocidad de Doncic y Ricky Rubio |url=https://www.marca.com/baloncesto/acb/2019/09/29/5d91177846163fb4138b462d.html |website=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]] |access-date=13 October 2019 |language=es |date=29 September 2019}} On 30 October 2019, Garuba made his [[EuroLeague]] debut, recording 12 points, four rebounds, three steals, and a [[Performance Index Rating]] (PIR) of 20, against [[FC Bayern Munich (basketball)|Bayern Munich]].{{cite web |last1=Zachari |first1=Antigoni |title=17-year-old Usman Garuba made his EuroLeague debut count |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/958918/17-year-old-usman-garuba-made-his-euroleague-debut-count/ |publisher=EuroHoops |access-date=2 November 2019 |date=31 October 2019}} He finished the season averaging 4.4 points, 4.4 rebounds and 0.7 blocks in 15 minutes per game in the ACB and EuroLeague and was an [[ACB Best Young Player Award|ACB All-Young Players Team]] selection.{{cite web |title=Mejor Quinteto Joven El Corte Inglés de la Liga Endesa 2019-20 |url=https://www.acb.com/articulo/ver/153499-mejor-quinteto-joven-el-corte-ingles-de-la-liga-endesa-201920.html |publisher=[[Liga ACB]] |access-date=27 June 2020 |language=es |date=25 June 2020}}{{cite web |title=Usman Garuba Player Profile |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Usman-Garuba/Summary/108741 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |access-date=27 June 2020}} On 22 December 2020, Garuba recorded 12 points, six rebounds, three assists and 25 PIR in a 91–62 win over [[Alba Berlin]].{{cite web |title=El Real Madrid gana con el mejor partido Euroliga de Garuba y otro recital de Tavares |url=https://www.gigantes.com/euroliga/el-real-madrid-gana-con-el-mejor-partido-euroliga-de-garuba-y-otro-recital-de-tavares/ |website=Gigantes del Basket |access-date=26 April 2021 |language=Spanish |date=22 December 2020}} On 18 April 2021, he posted 14 points and 12 rebounds in a 101–92 victory over Joventut Badalona.{{cite web |title=El coloso Usman Garuba se asoma al top 15 del draft con su mejor partido en la ACB |url=https://www.marca.com/baloncesto/acb/2021/04/19/607d4a99e2704eef178b45bc.html |website=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]] |access-date=26 April 2021 |language=Spanish |date=19 April 2021}} Garuba won the [[ACB Best Young Player Award]] and was named to the ACB All-Young Players Team for his second straight season.{{cite web |title=Usman Garuba, elegido Mejor Joven de la Liga Endesa 20-21 |url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/baloncesto/acb/20210426/493462838812/usman-garuba-elegido-mejor-joven-de-la-liga-endesa-20-21.html |website=[[Mundo Deportivo]] |access-date=26 April 2021 |language=Spanish |date=26 April 2021}} On 29 April, he recorded a career-high 24 points, 12 rebounds and 30 PIR, leading Real Madrid to an 82–76 win over [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]] in Game 4 of the [[2021 EuroLeague Playoffs|EuroLeague Playoffs]].{{cite web |title=Real's déjà vu rally evens series with Efes! |url=https://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=321&seasoncode=E2020#!report |publisher=[[EuroLeague]] |access-date=29 April 2021 |date=29 April 2021}} Garuba earned [[EuroLeague Rising Star]] honors after averaging 3.9 points and four rebounds per game in the competition.{{cite web |title=Rising Star Trophy winner: Usman Garuba, Real Madrid |url=https://www.euroleague.net/news/i/bip4dvrj4olwg33l/rising-star-trophy-winner-usman-garuba-real-madrid |publisher=[[EuroLeague]] |access-date=14 May 2021 |date=14 May 2021}} == National team career == Garuba made his junior national team debut for [[Spain national under-16 basketball team|Spain]] at the [[2016 FIBA U16 European Championship]] in [[Radom]], Poland. He was named MVP after leading his team to a gold medal and averaging 16.3 points, 12.4 rebounds, and a tournament-leading 2.9 blocks per game.{{cite web |title=Usman Garuba claims MVP award to lead All-Star Five |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u16/2016/news/usman-garuba-claims-mvp-award-to-lead-all-star-five |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=12 October 2019 |date=21 August 2016}} A 14-year-old and the second youngest player in the tournament, Garuba became the first player from a lower age group to ever win MVP at the event.{{cite web |last1=Schmitz |first1=Mike |title=FIBA U16 European Championship Scouting Reports |url=http://www.draftexpress.com/article/FIBA-U16-European-Championship-Scouting-Reports-5648/ |publisher=DraftExpress |access-date=13 October 2019 |date=22 August 2016}} After recording 15 points, 11 rebounds, and 10 blocks in the final against [[Lithuania men's national under-16 and under-17 basketball team|Lithuania]], he joined [[Dario Šarić]] and [[Ricky Rubio]] as the only players in history with a triple-double in the final of the tournament.{{cite web |title=Garuba happy to finally be back with his 2002 generation |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u16/2018/news/garuba-happy-to-finally-be-back-with-his-2002-generation |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=12 October 2019 |date=16 August 2018}} In the summer of 2017, Garuba was unable to return to national team duty because he was recovering from a knee injury suffered earlier that year. At the [[2018 FIBA U16 European Championship]] in [[Novi Sad]], Serbia, he averaged 16.3 points and 12.3 rebounds per game and led Spain to a silver medal, earning a spot on the All-Star Five.{{cite web |title="I told the coach to draw the last play up for me," says MVP Prkacin |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u16/2018/news/-i-told-the-coach-to-draw-the-last-play-up-for-me-says-mvp-prkacin |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=12 October 2019 |date=19 August 2018}} Garuba helped Spain win a gold medal at the [[2019 FIBA U18 European Championship]] in [[Volos]], Greece, joining his teammate and MVP [[Santi Aldama]] on the All-Star Five after averaging 15.6 points, 12.9 rebounds, and 2.1 blocks per game.{{cite web |title=Unstoppable Aldama headlines the All-Star Five of the FIBA U18 European Championship |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u18/2019/news/unstoppable-aldama-headlines-the-all-star-five-of-the-fiba-u18-european-championship |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=13 October 2019 |date=4 August 2019}} == Personal life == Garuba's parents are from [[Benin City]], Nigeria but left to escape conflict in their hometown. After initially moving to [[City of Brussels|Brussels]],{{cite web |last1=Sáez |first1=Faustino |title=Garuba, tras la estela de Doncic y Ricky Rubio |url=https://elpais.com/deportes/2019/09/30/actualidad/1569835058_370066.html |website=[[El País]] |access-date=10 October 2019 |language=es |date=30 September 2019}} they settled in Madrid in the 1990s without [[work permit]]s.{{cite web |last1=Mucha |first1=Martín |title=Los nuevos hermanos Gasol |url=https://www.elmundo.es/cronica/2016/12/08/5843e4c4e5fdeaa3558b4632.html |website=[[El Mundo (Spain)|El Mundo]] |access-date=10 October 2019 |language=es |date=8 December 2016}} His father, Mustapha, works for manufacturing company [[Grupo Bimbo|Bimbo]] in [[Guadalajara, Spain|Guadalajara]], and his mother, Betty, works for the Azuqueca employment program. Garuba has one younger brother, Sediq (b. 2004) and a younger sister, Uki (b. 2010). == References == {{Reflist}} == External links == *[https://www.realmadrid.com/en/basketball/usman-garuba Usman Garuba] at realmadrid.com {{Real Madrid Baloncesto current roster}} {{Euroleague Rising Star Award}} {{ACB Best Young Player Award}} {{FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship MVP Award}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Garuba, Usman}} [[Category:2002 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Basketball players at the 2020 Summer Olympics]] [[Category:Centers (basketball)]] [[Category:Liga ACB players]] [[Category:Olympic basketball players of Spain]] [[Category:Power forwards (basketball)]] [[Category:Real Madrid Baloncesto players]] [[Category:Spanish men's basketball players]] [[Category:Spanish sportspeople of African descent]] [[Category:Spanish people of Nigerian descent]] [[Category:Sportspeople of Nigerian descent]] [[Category:Basketball players from Madrid]]
